plan: 2 Kings 15:32-38; 2 Chronicles 27:1-9; Micah 1:1-16; 2 Kings 16:1-9; 2 Chronicles 28:1-15; Isaiah 7:1-9, 10-25

readings.title: The Reign of Jotham in Judah
readings.subtitle: He did what was right, but the high places remained, and Aram and Israel began to press against Judah.
readings.text: [2 Kings 15:32] In the second year of Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Yotham son of Uzziyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [33] He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yerusha the daughter of Tsaḏoq. [34] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>He</dn> did according to all that his father Uzziyahu did. [35] However, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. <dn>He</dn> built the Upper Gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [36] And the rest of the acts of Yotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [37] In those days <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began to send <dn>את</dn> Retsin sovereign of Aram and <dn>את</dn> Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu against Yehuḏah. [38] So Yotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ his father. And Aḥaz his son reigned in his place.

readings.section: The Prophets of the Divided Kingdom
readings.title: The Word of YeHoVaH to Micah
readings.subtitle: A prophecy of judgment against Samaria and Jerusalem for their transgressions and incurable wounds.
readings.text: [Micah 1:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that came to Miḵah of Moresheth in the days of Yotham, Aḥaz, Ḥizqiyah, sovereigns of Yehuḏah, which he saw concerning Shomeron and Yerushalayim. [2] Hear, all you peoples! Listen, O earth, and all who are in it! And let the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be a witness against you – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from <dn>His</dn> set-apart Hěḵal. [3] For look, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is coming out of <dn>His</dn> place, and <dn>He</dn> shall come down and shall tread on the high places of the earth. [4] And the mountains shall melt under <dn>Him</dn>, and the valleys be cleft as wax before the fire, as waters poured down a steep place. [5] All this is for the transgression of Ya‛aqoḇ and for the sins of the house of Yisra’ěl. What is the transgression of Ya‛aqoḇ? Is it not Shomeron? And what are the high places of Yehuḏah? Are they not Yerushalayim? [6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make Shomeron a heap in the field, places for planting a vineyard. And <dn>I</dn> shall pour down her stones into the valley, and uncover her foundations.</dq> [7] <dq>“And all her carved images shall be beaten in pieces, and all her harlot-fees be burned with the fire. And all her idols <dn>I</dn> shall lay waste, for she gathered it from the harlot-fee of a whore, and they shall return to the harlot-fee of a whore.”</dq> [8] Because of this I lament and howl. I go stripped and naked. I make a lamentation like jackals, and a mourning like ostriches. [9] For her wounds are incurable. For it has come to Yehuḏah, it has come to the gate of <dn>My</dn> people, to Yerushalayim.

readings.section: The Prophets of the Divided Kingdom
readings.title: Lamentation Over Judah's Cities
readings.subtitle: The coming judgment will bring shame, mourning, and exile to the towns of Judah.
readings.text: [Micah 1:10] Do not declare it in Gath, weep not at all in Běyth Aphrah, roll yourself in the dust. [11] Pass by in nakedness and shame, you inhabitant of Shaphir. The inhabitant of Tsa’anan has not gone out. The lamentation of Běyth Ětsel takes from you its standing place. [12] Though the inhabitants of Maroth waited for good, yet evil came down from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the gate of Yerushalayim. [13] O inhabitant of Laḵish, harness the chariot to the horse – she was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Tsiyon – for the transgressions of Yisra’ěl were found in you. [14] Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath, the houses of Aḵziḇ becoming a deception to the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. [15] <dq>Again <dn>I</dn> shall bring a dispossessor to you, O inhabitant of Marěshah. The esteem of Yisra’ěl shall come to Aḏullam.</dq> [16] Make yourself bald and cut off your hair for the children of your delight. Enlarge your baldness like an eagle, for they shall be exiled from you.

readings.title: The Wicked Reign of Ahaz
readings.subtitle: Ahaz walks in the ways of Israel's kings, faces attack, and appeals to Assyria for help.
readings.text: [2 Kings 16:1] In the seventeenth year of Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, Aḥaz son of Yotham, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [2] Aḥaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, as his father Daviḏ had done. [3] But he walked in the way of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl, and he also made <dn>את</dn> his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ěl. [4] And he slaughtered and burned incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree. [5] Then Retsin sovereign of Aram and Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, came up to Yerushalayim, to battle. And they besieged Aḥaz but were unable to overcome him. [6] At that time Retsin sovereign of Aram recovered <dn>את</dn> Ěylath for Aram, and drove the men of Yehuḏah from Ěylath. And the Eḏomites went to Ěylath, and have dwelt there to this day. [7] And Aḥaz sent messengers to Tiḡlath-Pileser sovereign of Ashshur, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the sovereign of Aram and from the hand of the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, who are rising up against me.” [8] And Aḥaz took <dn>את</dn> the silver and gold that was found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and in the treasuries of the house of the sovereign, and sent it as a present to the sovereign of Ashshur. [9] And the sovereign of Ashshur listened to him. And the sovereign of Ashshur went up against Dammeseq and captured it, and exiled it to Qir, and he killed <dn>את</dn> Retsin.

readings.section: The Prophets of the Divided Kingdom
readings.title: A Message of Reassurance to Ahaz
readings.subtitle: Isaiah is sent to tell Ahaz not to fear the alliance of Aram and Ephraim, for their plans will not stand.
readings.text: [Isaiah 7:1] And it came to be in the days of Aḥaz son of Yotham, son of Uzziyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, that Retsin sovereign of Aram and Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, went up to Yerushalayim to fight against it, but could not prevail against it. [2] And it was reported to the house of Daviḏ, saying, “Aram has set up camp in Ephrayim.” And his heart and the heart of his people were moved as the trees of the forest are moved with the wind. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yeshayahu, <dq>“Go out now to meet Aḥaz, you and She’ar-Yashuḇ your son, at the end of the channel of the upper pool, on the highway of the Launderer’s Field,</dq> [4] <dq>and say to him, ‘Take heed, and be calm; do not fear or be faint-hearted for these two stubs of smoking firebrands, for the fierce displeasure of Retsin and Aram, and the son of Remalyahu.</dq> [5] <dq>Because Aram, Ephrayim, and the son of Remalyahu have plotted evil against you, saying,</dq> [6] <dq>“Let us go up against Yehuḏah and tear it apart, and break it open for ourselves, and set a sovereign over them, <dn>את</dn> the son of Taḇe’ěl.”</dq> [7] <dq>Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “It is not going to stand, nor shall it take place.</dq> [8] <dq>“For the head of Aram is Dammeseq, and the head of Dammeseq is Retsin. And within sixty-five years Ephrayim is to be broken as a people.</dq> [9] <dq>“And the head of Ephrayim is Shomeron, and the head of Shomeron is the son of Remalyahu. If you do not believe, you are not steadfast.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.section: The Prophets of the Divided Kingdom
readings.title: The Sign of Immanuel
readings.subtitle: When Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, YeHoVaH gives the sign of the 'almah' who will conceive and bear a son.
readings.text: [Isaiah 7:10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke again to Aḥaz, saying, [11] <dq>“Ask a sign for yourself from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>; make deep the request or make it high.”</dq> [12] But Aḥaz said, “I do not ask nor try <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!” [13] And he said, “Hear now, O house of Daviḏ! Is it not enough that you weary men, that you weary <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> also? [14] “Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> gives you a sign: Look, the ‘almah’ conceives and gives birth to a son, and shall call <dn>His</dn> Name Immanu’ěl. [15] “<dn>He</dn> eats curds and honey when <dn>He</dn> knows to refuse evil and choose the good. [16] “For before the child knows to refuse evil and choose the good, the land that you dread is to be forsaken by both her sovereigns. [17] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings on you and your people and your father’s house days that have not come since the day that Ephrayim turned away from Yehuḏah – <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ashshur.”

readings.section: The Prophets of the Divided Kingdom
readings.title: The Razor from Beyond the River
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH will whistle for Egypt and Assyria, who will desolate the land, leaving it to thornbushes and weeds.
readings.text: [Isaiah 7:18] And it shall be in that day that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> whistles for the fly that is in the farthest part of the rivers of Mitsrayim, and for the bee that is in the land of Ashshur. [19] And they shall come, and all of them shall rest in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all weeds and in all pastures. [20] In that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall shave with a razor hired beyond the River – with the sovereign of Ashshur – <dn>את</dn> the head and the hair of the legs, and also remove <dn>את</dn> the beard. [21] And it shall be in that day that a man keeps alive a young cow and two sheep. [22] And it shall be, that he shall eat curds because of the plenty milk he gets, for everyone left in the land shall eat curds. [23] And it shall be in that day, every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand sheqels of silver, let it be for thornbushes and weeds. [24] With arrows and bows one shall go there, because all the land shall be thornbushes and weeds. [25] And to all the hills which were tilled with the hoe, you do not go for fear of thornbushes and weeds; but it shall be for sending oxen to, and a place for sheep to roam.
